arguments.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one original adult humanoid FRONT DESIGN REFERENCE, proposed source-only companion concept. Single figure, single front view, portrait canvas.
Primary request: Design an original adult wandering bard and ranged support companion, a slim expressive man in his early thirties with wavy chestnut hair, a warm intelligent face, a small playful smile and a jaunty burgundy feathered cap. Teal velvet doublet with restrained muted-gold braid and small original leaf-and-knot embroidery, burgundy puff sleeves, fitted burgundy trousers, dark worn leather boots. Distinct original face and costume, no actor likeness and no reproduction of existing franchise key art.
Reference guidance: The previously inspected Geralt owner reference guides only the serious premium fantasy-miniature cohort, dark neutral presentation, convincing cloth/leather/metal, and restrained aged-metal accents. Do not copy Geralt's identity, white hair, scars, yellow eyes, armor, wolf pendant or swords. The inspected Medusa quality reference guides polished sculptural realism, readable anatomy and rich material definition only; do not copy its subject, costume, snakes, bow or elevated camera. This bard's teal and burgundy cloth is his distinct palette.
Pose and hands: strict FRONT orthographic, face looking directly forward, chest and pelvis squared to camera, shoulders level, both feet pointing forward and both boots entirely visible. Relaxed naturally bent arms, no combat gesture. Hold ONE complete wooden lute visibly beside the body, offset toward the man's left side (image right) rather than hiding the torso or legs. Anatomical RIGHT hand gently holds the lute neck; anatomical LEFT hand supports the lower lute body from underneath. Arrange the lute diagonally enough that both hands are visible from the front with each thumb and all four fingers individually readable and naturally attached. The neck hand must not conceal its thumb behind the neck. Palm-support fingers spread slightly along the near lower edge of the instrument. Show the complete neck, tuning pegs, strings, soundboard and lower bowl silhouette. No hand fused to instrument or sleeve. Preserve plain charcoal negative-space gaps around elbows and between arms and torso, and a gap between legs. Instruments and hand contacts are the only intentional overlaps.
Composition/framing: one full figure from feather tip to boot soles, no cropping. Exact frontal orthographic camera at the midpoint of the figure, no perspective, no three-quarter rotation and no camera looking down. Center the combined figure-and-lute silhouette. Keep the highest feather tip at 6% of total image height and the bottom of the pedestal at 90%, leaving 10% plain background below it; leave generous side margins around the whole instrument and every limb.
Pedestal: ONE round dark stone pedestal made of exactly TWO stacked low circular discs, viewed perfectly EDGE-ON. Show only the two vertical front side bands separated by one thin seam, straight horizontal upper and lower edges. No visible top surface, no ellipse, no foot-shaped ground plane, no scenic ground. Both boots meet the upper horizontal edge. Do not imitate the visible pedestal top in either quality reference.
Style/medium: premium realistic painted fantasy miniature design render with crisp sculptural silhouette, tactile velvet, subtle gold braid, fine lute wood grain and readable adult anatomy. Soft neutral studio lighting, even enough to read the hands and face; gentle natural material shading, no dramatic rim halo. Single plain uniform charcoal background.
Constraints: Exactly one adult human bard, two arms, two hands with five digits each, two legs, one complete lute, one two-disc stone pedestal. No extra props, no weapons, no companion animal. No VFX, magical aura, glow, smoke, motion trails, particles, ground scene, landscape, captions, text, labels, numbers, watermarks, logos, UI or multi-view sheet. No copying actor likeness, commercial scans, franchise costume or game-key-art composition. This is a new original concept, not an edit of either reference.
